title: Building America's Capacity to Innovate
gist: Forum repost of an Intel Foundry piece by Naga Chandrasekaran arguing Intel is building U.S. semiconductor R&D and manufacturing capacity; cites SIA data that the U.S. share of semiconductor manufacturing fell from 37% to 10% between 1990 and 2022. Largely promotional excerpt.

insights.claim: According to the Semiconductor Industry Association, the share of semiconductors manufactured in the United States declined from 37% to 10% between 1990 and 2022.
insights.speaker: P
insights.so_what: Quantifies the reshoring gap underpinning U.S. industrial policy support for domestic fabs.
insights.quote: the share manufactured in the United States declined from 37% to 10% between 1990 and 2022

insights.claim: Intel Foundry's Naga Chandrasekaran argues that semiconductor leadership will determine whether America continues to drive global prosperity through technology for the next 250 years.
insights.speaker: P
insights.so_what: Intel positions itself as a national-champion beneficiary of U.S. policy support.
insights.quote: Semiconductor leadership will help determine whether America continues to do so for the next 250 years.

insights.claim: Intel presents itself as building the U.S. capacity needed for the next era of innovation, spanning R&D through high-volume manufacturing.
insights.speaker: P
insights.so_what: Signals Intel's continued emphasis on domestic HVM as a strategic and political selling point.
insights.quote: Intel is helping build the capacity America needs for the next era of innovation.

insights.claim: Intel Foundry states that demand for computing power is growing at an unprecedented pace, requiring some of the most advanced R&D, engineering and manufacturing work ever undertaken.
insights.speaker: P
insights.so_what: Reinforces the compute-demand narrative supporting foundry capex.
insights.quote: Demand for computing power is growing at an unprecedented pace.
